title: Graded compatibility and isomorphism detection for already given filtered lifts
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. For $\mathcal C=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, let $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ be the localization of bounded-below complexes with a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. Write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal C)$ for the full subcategory whose graded pieces vanish outside the integers $a\le p\le b$. Suppose exact functors $G_i:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ have already been equipped with exact filtered lifts $\widetilde G_i:DF^+(\mathcal A)\to DF^+(\mathcal B)$ preserving every interval $[a,b]$. Here an exact filtered lift means an exact functor with $\widetilde G_i(DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal A))\subseteq DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal B)$ together with a natural isomorphism $\phi_i:\omega\widetilde G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\omega$. Then there are canonical natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{gr}^p\widetilde G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\operatorname{gr}^p$ for every $p$. If a natural transformation $h:G_1\to G_2$ has already been supplied with a filtered lift, meaning a natural transformation $\widetilde h:\widetilde G_1\to\widetilde G_2$ satisfying $\phi_2\circ\omega\widetilde h=(h\omega)\circ\phi_1$, then these graded comparisons identify $\operatorname{gr}^p\widetilde h$ with $h\operatorname{gr}^p$. If $h$ is an isomorphism, $\widetilde h$ is an isomorphism. These comparisons are compatible with identity transformations, composition of already lifted transformations, and composition of filtered functors. This asserts properties of supplied lifts, not existence of a lift of an arbitrary ordinary natural transformation.

source.place: §5.1.3(a),(b),(e) and Lemma 5.1.4(i)–(iii), pp.39–41; the covariant single-functor case, restricted to bounded-below finite filtrations.

proof.text: Fix $i,r,M$. Use the universal truncations of [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle]. Exactness of $\widetilde G_i$ sends the truncation triangle to a distinguished triangle with middle vertex $\widetilde G_iM$. Its first vertex is supported in degrees $\ge r$ and its last in degrees $<r$: both truncated inputs have finite filtration support, so the stated preservation of every finite interval applies. Uniqueness of the supported truncation triangle gives isomorphisms $\sigma^{\ge}_{i,r,M}:\widetilde G_i t_{\ge r}M\to t_{\ge r}\widetilde G_iM$ and $\sigma^{<}_{i,r,M}:\widetilde G_i t_{<r}M\to t_{<r}\widetilde G_iM$, characterized by $\iota_{r,\widetilde G_iM}\sigma^{\ge}_{i,r,M}=\widetilde G_i(\iota_{r,M})$ and $\sigma^{<}_{i,r,M}\widetilde G_i(q_{r,M})=q_{r,\widetilde G_iM}$. These characterizations determine each map uniquely by the two Hom bijections in the cited statement. For any $v:M\to N$, the two possible composites with the subcomplex comparison have the same composite with $\iota_{r,\widetilde G_iN}$ by naturality of $\iota$; the Hom bijection makes them equal. For the quotient comparison, precomposition with $\widetilde G_i(q_{r,M})$ gives equality by naturality of $q$. This precomposition is injective on maps into the low-supported target: $\widetilde G_i(q_{r,M})=(\sigma^{<}_{i,r,M})^{-1}q_{r,\widetilde G_iM}$, so the quotient Hom bijection and invertibility of $\sigma^{<}_{i,r,M}$ apply. Thus both comparisons are natural, without choosing a cone map.

source.place: §5.1.2(c) and proof of Lemma 5.1.4(i), unary filtration-truncation argument

proof.text: For $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$ from [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle], compose the comparisons of Step 1 to obtain $\kappa_{i,p,M}=t_{\ge p}(\sigma^{<}_{i,p+1,M})\circ\sigma^{\ge}_{i,p,t_{<p+1}M}:\widetilde G_iT_pM\xrightarrow{\sim}T_p\widetilde G_iM$. Since $\omega T_p=\operatorname{gr}^p$ naturally, define $\theta^p_{i,M}=\phi_{i,T_pM}\circ\omega(\kappa_{i,p,M}^{-1}):\operatorname{gr}^p\widetilde G_iM\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\operatorname{gr}^pM$. Each factor is a natural isomorphism, so this proves the first clause. On an object supported only in degree $p$, the truncation maps identify $T_p$ with the identity, and this formula becomes the supplied forgetful comparison. The formula uses fixed truncation functors and no choice of finite bounds.

Write $\alpha=\widetilde h$. Naturality of $\alpha$ for $\iota_{r,M}$ shows that $t_{\ge r}(\alpha_M)\sigma^{\ge}_{1,r,M}$ and $\sigma^{\ge}_{2,r,M}\alpha_{t_{\ge r}M}$ have the same composite with $\iota_{r,\widetilde G_2M}$. Their source is supported in degrees $\ge r$, so the first Hom bijection of [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle] proves equality. Likewise naturality for $q_{r,M}$ makes $t_{<r}(\alpha_M)\sigma^{<}_{1,r,M}$ and $\sigma^{<}_{2,r,M}\alpha_{t_{<r}M}$ equal after precomposition with $\widetilde G_1(q_{r,M})$; the quotient Hom bijection and the isomorphism $\sigma^{<}_{1,r,M}$ prove equality. Combining these two equations gives $T_p(\alpha_M)\kappa_{1,p,M}=\kappa_{2,p,M}\alpha_{T_pM}$. Apply $\omega$, invert the two $\kappa$ maps, and use the hypothesized equation $\phi_{2,T_pM}\omega(\alpha_{T_pM})=h_{\omega T_pM}\phi_{1,T_pM}$. The result is exactly $\theta^p_{2,M}\operatorname{gr}^p(\widetilde h_M)=h_{\operatorname{gr}^pM}\theta^p_{1,M}$. This proves transformation compatibility directly, using no faithfulness of the forgetful functor.

If $h$ is invertible, Step 3 makes every $\operatorname{gr}^p(\widetilde h_M)$ invertible. Choose a distinguished cone triangle of $\widetilde h_M$. Exactness of each graded functor [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle] and the zero-cone criterion [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] show that every grade of its cone $C$ is zero. Represent $C$ by a bounded-below finite-filtered complex $K$: every $\operatorname{gr}^pK$ is acyclic, hence $K\to0$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism and is inverted by the defining localization. Thus $C=0$, and the same zero-cone criterion in $DF^+(\mathcal B)$ gives invertibility of $\widetilde h_M$. This holds for every $M$, proving the isomorphism clause.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.4(iii); §5.1.2(a,b); zero-cone criterion also Stacks Tag 05QR, lemma-third-object-zero

proof.text: For identities and composites of supplied transformations, Step 3 says each graded transformation is conjugation of its ordinary transformation by the fixed $\theta$ maps. Conjugating an identity yields an identity; for two transformations the intermediate $\theta^{-1}\theta$ cancels, giving compatibility with their composition. For filtered-functor composition, let $\mathcal E$ be a third abelian category, and let $(\widetilde F,\phi_F)$, with $\widetilde F:DF^+(\mathcal A)\to DF^+(\mathcal B)$, and $(\widetilde H,\phi_H)$, with $\widetilde H:DF^+(\mathcal B)\to DF^+(\mathcal E)$, be supplied interval-preserving exact filtered lifts of exact functors $F$ and $H$, as in the statement. The composite $\sigma^{\ge}_{H,r,\widetilde F M}\circ\widetilde H(\sigma^{\ge}_{F,r,M})$ has composite with $\iota_{r,\widetilde H\widetilde F M}$ equal to $\widetilde H\widetilde F(\iota_{r,M})$, so the universal Hom bijection [lem-trf-filtered-truncation-triangle] identifies it with $\sigma^{\ge}_{HF,r,M}$. Similarly $\sigma^{<}_{H,r,\widetilde F M}\circ\widetilde H(\sigma^{<}_{F,r,M})$ is $\sigma^{<}_{HF,r,M}$ by its quotient equation. Using naturality of $\sigma^{\ge}_{H,p}$ from Step 1 for $\sigma^{<}_{F,p+1,M}$, therefore $\kappa_{HF,p,M}=\kappa_{H,p,\widetilde F M}\circ\widetilde H(\kappa_{F,p,M})$. Take the composite forgetful comparison to be $H(\phi_{F,M})\circ\phi_{H,\widetilde F M}$. Substitute the displayed $\kappa$ equality in Step 2 and apply naturality of $\phi_H$ to $\kappa_F^{-1}$. This gives $\theta^p_{HF,M}=H(\theta^p_{F,M})\circ\theta^p_{H,\widetilde F M}$, with the canonical functor-composition identifications. Identity filtered functors have identity $\sigma,\kappa$, so the formula also respects identities. All coherence assertions use these specified composite lift structures.
